what: Encrypted-JS-with-runtime-decryption is NOT a real product category in 2026. Every commercial "JS encryption" tool (Jscrambler, JSDefender, KlassMaster, PreEmptive) is obfuscation with marketing paint. Fundamental problem: decryption key must execute where attacker observes it. PreEmptive's own engineers: "since the app must use the key at runtime, it's still accessible with tools like browser DevTools via breakpoints, function hooking, or variable tracing." Autodesk's WASM+key experiment hardcodes the key in source and admits attackers can extract it. TPM / Secure Enclave CAN protect per-device provisioned keys (SSH, FairPlay) but not shipping format — would require a DRM backend with per-device provisioning, nobody has productized this for JS. Code virtualization (JSVMP) is stronger than plain obfuscation but reversible via VM dispatcher analysis. Bytenode bypassed by PT SWARM Ghidra plugin. ONLY path that genuinely raises reverse-engineering cost: rewrite sensitive logic in Rust via napi-rs, ship compiled .node binary via npm optionalDependencies (Sentry, esbuild, swc, Turbo, Biome, Rspack, Rolldown, lightningcss all do this). Takes RE cost from hours → days-weeks. Everything else in JS-land is friction, not security.
why: User asked "has no one invented encryption-key + decrypt at runtime" — comprehensive agent research confirmed this is vaporware despite many commercial claims. Worth documenting so future spawns don't chase the "encrypted JS" dead end. The napi-rs pattern is the only real escape hatch beyond obfuscation tier.
